purpose: Freeze the code-domain benchmark execution order before adding reviewer-facing Stage-C benchmark outcomes.

claim_boundary.current_supported_claim: Code-domain equal-token curation has completed payload readiness and held-out NLL validation.
claim_boundary.block3_additional_claim_if_passed: Curated code-domain fine-tuning transfers to lightweight code-generation benchmarks without required retention guardrail regression.
claim_boundary.forbidden_claim_until_swebench_and_nonco: The framework is generally validated for agentic software engineering or non-code LM training corpora.

utility_scope: All benchmark outcomes are Stage-C validation evidence only and are forbidden from Stage-B selector objectives.

benchmark_tiers.role: Primary next code-domain external benchmark family because it is cheaper and less agentic than SWE-bench.

success_rule.metric: macro EvalPlus pass-rate across HumanEval+ and MBPP+
success_rule.guardrail_rule: No required confirmatory retention guardrail may fail.
success_rule.inconclusive_action: Report as inconclusive; do not tune Stage B using benchmark outcomes.

benchmark_tiers.role: High-cost capstone for agentic software engineering evidence, not the first proof of the curation framework.
required_feasibility_gate: Docker or equivalent isolated execution confirmed
storage and runtime budget confirmed outside C drive pressure
agentic patch-generation harness frozen before outcomes
benchmark task split frozen before outcomes
benchmark task content quarantined away from Stage-B artifacts
local versus cloud execution surface decided before outcomes

success_rule.missing_or_infeasible_action: Keep paper claim bounded to NLL plus EvalPlus evidence.

forbidden_uses: using EvalPlus, HumanEval+, MBPP+, SWE-bench, NLL, or retention outcomes inside Stage-B selector objectives
changing Stage-B policy after seeing Stage-C benchmark outcomes
changing benchmark margins after seeing benchmark outcomes
using benchmark task content as candidate training data
claiming production-grade curation from tier1 results alone
next_actions: Run tier1 EvalPlus sample generation for all trained code-domain arms and frozen seeds.
Run isolated EvalPlus evaluation for HumanEval+ and MBPP+.
Build a tier1 benchmark comparison report with raw, Stage-A random, curated, and high-quality reference arms.
Only after tier1 is complete, decide whether SWE-bench feasibility is worth the compute and storage cost.
